data.title: Robots Showcase Industrial Potential at Shanghai Expo as Global Tie-Ups Address Industry Gaps
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 16 -- Humanoid robots are taking center stage at this year’s China International Industry Fair in Shanghai, as Chinese and international companies link arms to build a stronger industrial ecosystem and accelerate their deployment on factory floors.

At this year’s CIIF, which ended today, a number of humanoid robots and embodied artificial intelligence solutions demonstrated their ability to carry out precision manufacturing tasks. Shanghai-based AgiBot’s Genie G2 robot, for example, can perform millimeter-level insertion and removal operations involving optical modules. It can also be deployed across an entire production line in just two to three hours.

Taipei-based Delta Electronics unveiled a dual-arm collaborative robotics solution powered by US chipmaker Nvidia’s computing platform, designed to handle non-standard, complex assembly processes such as AI server assembly.

China’s humanoid robotics technology is currently among the global front-runners, but the industry continues to face major bottlenecks such as a shortage of industrial data, insufficient computing power and an underdeveloped supply chain.

To address some of these issues, Germany’s Siemens announced that it will open five factories in China and six industrial application scenarios for on-site training and validation of embodied AI systems, while fellow German firm Bosch Rexroth has also set up a dedicated project team and opened production-line workstations to allow robotics companies to collect training data.

At the computing-power level, beyond Santa Clara-based Nvidia’s Thor platform, which has been adopted by several high-end robots, Chinese chip solutions are moving more rapidly toward commercial deployment.

D-Robotics’ Xuri S600 chip has been adapted for use by more than 20 robotics manufacturers. Its applications include industrial welding and power infrastructure inspections, with most projects having moved to mass production and shipment. Meanwhile, Axera Semiconductor has launched a high-performance edge AI chip which when paired with its self-developed embodied AI brain, enables industrial tasks such as electronic assembly and flexible cutting.

Key Bottlenecks

Data and computing power remain the two of the sector’s biggest challenges.

Industrial data is fragmented and often kept within closed systems, said Wang Jian, a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Engineering. Limited data sharing is also constraining the iterative improvement of robotics technology.

Even with high-end computing platforms, the industry continues to face a widespread shortage of computing resources, said a representative from Shenzhen-based D-Robotics.

The ongoing development and refinement of embodied AI models will sustain high demand for computing power over the long term. The complexity of industrial environments adds another challenge. Production lines often combine older equipment with newer machinery, making data alignment difficult. The industry is still working to improve the effective utilization of available data.

Industry insiders believe that humanoid robots at this stage can only perform well-defined, predictable tasks in factories. Their ability to adapt to complex and changing real-world working conditions remains the biggest hurdle to widespread commercial deployment.

Although humanoid robots have yet to be deployed at scale in factories, multinational companies are continuing to open their production lines for training and testing, while Chinese chipmakers are narrowing the technological gap.

With closer collaboration across the global industrial chain, large-scale deployment of humanoid robots in industrial settings is becoming an increasingly realistic prospect.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: China's Top Cities Complete Housing Sales Reform Rollout as Shenzhen Moves to Curb Unfinished Projects
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 16 -- China's four first-tier cities, including Shanghai and Guangzhou, have all issued new housing sales rules, with Shenzhen the last to do so, accelerating a shift away from a pre-sales model that has left buyers vulnerable to unfinished projects.

Shenzhen's rules, released yesterday, cover tighter management of housing pre-sales, promotion of completed home sales, and adjustments to land supply. Moreover, Hangzhou, a tech hub in eastern China, issued trial implementation rules for the new housing sales policy yesterday.

Industry insiders said that despite differences in the detailed measures adopted by individual cities, the overall direction is clear: requirements for acquiring land and selling homes will become stricter, and the transition toward sales of completed homes is accelerating.

The measures follow a nationwide reform package introduced on Aug. 28 to address risks in China's housing pre-sales model, under which developers sell homes before completion and use buyers' payments to finance construction. Financial difficulties at some developers have led to delays and unfinished projects, prompting authorities to tighten financing rules, protect homebuyers, and promote sales of completed homes.

The reforms follow the principle of applying existing rules to older projects and new requirements to future developments, although some cities have yet to clarify how the transition will work.

Shenzhen Prioritizes Completed Home Sales

Shenzhen is taking a gradual approach to completed home sales, while allowing developers to collect larger deposits from buyers than Beijing.

Under the southeastern city's new policy, developers acquiring residential land after Aug. 28 will be encouraged to sell homes only after construction is completed. This will be mandatory if specified in the government's land sale conditions. Developers must register sales of completed homes with the authorities and can collect deposits of up to 3 percent of the total home price after obtaining construction permits.

Sun Hongmei, a senior analyst at the Shenzhen branch of the China Index Academy, said Shenzhen is steadily advancing sales of completed homes through land supply policies. The city's 3 percent deposit cap matches Shanghai's, is more flexible than Beijing's 1 percent limit, and is more cautious than Guangzhou's 5 percent ceiling, striking a balance between developers' sales needs and homebuyers' financial security.

Regarding existing projects, Beijing, Guangzhou, and Tianjin have adopted a consistent approach, allowing developments already under construction to continue operating under the previous pre-sale rules, said Li Yujia, chief researcher at the Guangdong Housing Policy Research Center.

Shenzhen, like Shanghai, has left the treatment of such projects to further study by the relevant authorities, Li noted, adding that supporting measures have yet to be clarified.

Land Payment Rules Tightened

The rules also give developers more time to pay for land, but require full payment before they can begin pre-sales.

Shenzhen requires developers acquiring newly transferred residential land to make an initial payment of 50 percent of the land premium, with the balance generally due within one year. The payment period may be extended to two years for special projects.

Developers must pay the land premium in full before they can complete the initial land registration and obtain pre-sale permits for the first batch of homes.

Sun said that allowing land premiums to be paid in installments provides a buffer against tighter regulations and moderately eases developers' upfront financial burden.

Unlike Beijing, which allows land premiums to be paid over two years without directly linking payment to pre-sale eligibility, Shenzhen makes full payment a prerequisite for obtaining pre-sale permits, imposing stricter constraints to contain risks, she added.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China's CIIE to Set New Records for Exhibitors, Exhibition Space This Year as Product Debuts Surge
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 16 -- The Ninth China International Import Expo, which will be held in Shanghai next month, is poised to set new records for exhibitor numbers and exhibition space, with record highs also expected in the participation of leading companies and the number of products making their debut.

A total of 4,142 overseas firms from 162 countries and regions as well as international organizations will participate in the expo, which runs from Nov. 5 to Nov. 10, Vice Minister of Commerce Yan Dong said at a press conference today. Total exhibition space will exceed 440,000 square meters for the first time.

Launched in 2018, the CIIE is the world’s first national-level expo dedicated to imports. It comprises three main sections, namely the Country Exhibition, the Enterprise & Business Exhibition, and the Hongqiao International Economic Forum. The event serves as a platform for international procurement, investment promotion, people-to-people exchanges and broader cooperation.

This year’s Business Exhibition will occupy more than 370,000 square meters for the first time, Yan said. The number of Fortune Global 500 companies and industry-leading businesses participating will top 300, a new high, while more than 2,000 companies will be first-time exhibitors. And over 480 featured products will make their global, Asian or Chinese debuts at this year’s expo, also a record, he added.

In the Business Exhibition, companies from the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom and France will account for the largest exhibition areas. US firms will occupy more than 50,000 square meters, an increase of 1,500 square meters from last year, retaining the top spot for the eighth consecutive edition, Yan said.

The Country Exhibition will feature 69 countries and international organizations. Canada and Sri Lanka will serve as countries of honor. Five countries, including Moldova and Romania, as well as the United Nations Development Programme, will participate for the first time, Yan said.

Shanghai is positioning the “debut economy” as a key driver in its development into an international consumption center, Vice Mayor Lu Shan said at the press conference. Since 2018, the megacity has leveraged the CIIE as a platform to introduce more than 30,000 new products making their first market debut. It has also attracted more than 1,700 brands to open their first stores globally, in Asia or in China in Shanghai, Lu added.

Shanghai will host a series of product launch events during this year’s CIIE, while also extending opportunities for product debuts to the Yangtze River Delta region, where Shanghai is located, Lu said. These initiatives are intended to encourage supply-side innovation and spur consumption.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Kim Taylor

data.title: ChaPanda Says Chinese Tea Chain Is Cooperating With Investigation on Suspected IPO Manipulation
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 16 -- After Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission suspended ChaPanda shares from trading over artificial manipulation concerns surrounding its initial public offering, the Chinese new-style tea brand said it is fully cooperating with the relevant investigation.

Production and operations remain normal, Chengdu-based ChaPanda announced late on Oct. 14. Regulators have not disclosed specific details on the investigation's progress or findings yet, nor have they clarified whether anyone inside the company was involved.

The securities watchdog suspended ChaPanda's shares on Oct. 13, just five days after the firm announced a share incentive plan, citing concerns that the IPO may have been artificially manipulated to create a false impression of demand because part of the proceeds may have been diverted away from the company under undisclosed agreements with a suspicious group.

In plain terms, participating investors allegedly paid to subscribe for ChaPanda shares to create the illusion of "strong IPO demand," while the company secretly channeled its IPO proceeds back to the main subscribing investors after listing.

Artificially manipulating an IPO and fabricating fake subscription enthusiasm would lead ordinary investors to subscribe for or trade shares at unreasonable valuations, Shen Meng, executive director of Chanson Capital, told Yicai. If found to be fraudulent, ChaPanda could face criminal prosecution and civil lawsuits from Hong Kong investors, in addition to possible fines and delisting, bringing enormous risks, Shen added.

ChaPanda's trading suspension has little to do with its business operations and more with regulators investigating whether its IPO was artificially manipulated, industry insiders pointed out. In the first half of this year, the company's net profit rose 3.5 percent to CNY345 million (USD51.6 million) from a year ago, while its revenue jumped 6.2 percent to CNY2.7 billion (USD403.5 million).

ChaPanda's IPO in April 2024 was not exactly "hot." It initially planned to issue about 148 million shares, with no cornerstone investors introduced, allocating 10 percent to the Hong Kong public offering for retail investors and the rest to international institutional placement. However, the former was ultimately subscribed only 0.5 times, compared with 195 times for peer Guming Holdings and 3,617 times for Auntea Jenny. ChaPanda raised HKD2.6 billion (USD331.3 million) in its global offering.

In addition, ChaPanda had compelling reasons for going public.

In 2023, ChaPanda completed two rounds of pre-IPO capital increases, raising CNY970 million in institutional investment, using the funds for daily operations and the supply chain, with about 64 percent deployed before the IPO. However, investors held redemption rights, giving them the right to demand a share buyback if ChaPanda ultimately failed to go public, placing enormous repurchase pressure on the company.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Chinese Scientists Use Shanghai AI Lab's Scientific Model to Solve First World-Class Match Problem
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 16 -- A research team led by Xu Disheng, a professor at Great Bay University, has used a scientific multimodal artificial intelligence model developed by Shanghai AI Laboratory to prove the three-dimensional Ghys conjecture, marking the first time a domestic AI model has solved a world-class mathematical problem.

The proof of the Ghys conjecture, which has puzzled the mathematical community for 30 years, was completed using Intern-S2, Shanghai AI Lab announced yesterday. A team led by Dong Bin, a professor at Peking University, and Liu Ruochuan, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, has verified the findings, it added.

The paper on the proof has been published on the preprint platform arXiv, while the formal code was made available to the public on the code-sharing platform GitHub.

The Ghys conjecture, proposed by French mathematician Etienne Ghys in 1995, asks whether the behavior of chaotic dynamical systems can determine their geometric classification. It has long been regarded as a key open question in dynamical systems and a benchmark for testing mathematical reasoning capabilities.

A student of Fields Medal winner Artur Avila, Xu has long committed to proving the Ghys conjecture. After noticing the potential of AI models in math research last year, he visited the Shanghai AI Lab and formed a team that began collaborative research on model training at the start of this year.

Intern-S2, the result of the team upgrading the previous-generation Intern-S1, began exploring the Ghys conjecture from multiple angles in August, producing thousands of pages of derivations, based on which Xu and his partners continuously provided feedback to the model, corrected reverse exploration‌, and successfully found the proof method through multiple rounds of human-computer interaction.

The significance of this study lies in verifying a new scientific research paradigm, which is different from traditional math research that relies on long exploration by individual geniuses, Shanghai AI Lab pointed out. The proof systematically integrates expert intuition into the computer solving loop and creates a closed loop of "system exploration -- expert judgment -- achievement accumulation -- feedback correction," it added.

This paradigm can be replicated and used in more basic research fields with "huge search space but scarce experts" to achieve more original innovation breakthroughs from 0 to 1, the lab stressed.

AI's role in math research has attracted widespread attention. OpenAI said it spent 88 hours using 10,000 AI agents to solve the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem last month, while releasing 722 mathematical manuscripts covering multiple fields, including number theory, geometry, and algebra, earlier this month.

However, OpenAI's radical attempts have sparked controversy within the industry. After the US firm announced a proof of the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem, 25 Fields Medal winners, including Terence Chi-Shen Tao and Deng Yu, said that AI companies treat solving math problems as benchmark tests, which harms the mathematical community.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: China’s Naura to Buy Semiconductor Packaging Equipment Startup for USD61 Million
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 16 -- Leading Chinese semiconductor equipment supplier Naura Technology Group will invest CNY405 million (USD60.5 million) to buy a semiconductor packaging equipment startup that has not yet achieved mass production.

Naura yesterday signed an equity transfer agreement with a Beijing-based integrated circuit industry investment fund to acquire a 100 percent stake in Beijing Nuohe Jianwei Equipment to form synergies with its existing business and improve its ability to serve customers, the Beijing-based buyer announced on the same day.

Nuohe Jianwei’s core product is a semiconductor hybrid bonding equipment for advanced packaging, mainly used for three-dimensional integrated packaging of advanced chip products, such as system-on-a-chip, High Bandwidth Memory, and chiplets.

Nuohe Jianwei has key technological capabilities of hybrid bonding equipment production and has made products that have achieved nanometer-level precision alignment and received repeated orders, Naura noted. Nuohe Jianwei is cooperating with top clients to carry out equipment verification and negotiating for intent orders, showing strong market competitiveness and good development prospects.

However, because Nuohe Jianwei’s core products are still in the technological evolution, validation, and market introduction stage, the company has low revenue and remains in the red due to heavy research and development investment, according to Naura.

Nuohe Jianwei reported net losses of CNY29.9 million (USD4.5 million) last year and CNY9.4 million (USD1.4 million) in the first half of this year. It had CNY311 million in net assets at the end of the first half.

The hybrid bonding equipment market is experiencing rapid growth, as advanced packaging is reshaping the market landscape of semiconductor back-end devices, according to research firm Yole Group. Hybrid bonding is one of the fastest-growing segments and is expected to reach USD397 million by 2030, with a compound annual growth rate of over 21 percent.

Naura launched the Qomola HPD30, a 12-inch die-to-wafer hybrid bonding equipment, in March. According to the company’s semiannual financial statement, this equipment can be used in various scenarios, such as wafer-level 3D integration and heterogeneous chip integration, and has completed client verification and obtained mass orders.

Naura’s shares [SHE: 002371] were trading down 2.7 percent at CNY593.27 (USD88.69) as of 2.20 p.m. in Shenzhen today.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Futura Costaglione

data.title: High-Tech Firms Make Up Half of Exhibitors at First Phase of Canton Fair's Fall Edition
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 16 -- About 6,000 of the 12,000 exhibitors at the first phase of this year's fall leg of the bi-annual China Import and Export Fair, better known as the Canton Fair, are cutting-edge high-tech companies.

The 140th Canton Fair opened yesterday, with the first phase focusing on global sourcing hotspots, including energy, smart manufacturing, and embodied intelligence. The event features service robots, drones, display technologies, and 14 other emerging future industry zones, aiming to show overseas buyers the coordinated development of China's advanced manufacturing supply chain and the commercialization of technological innovation.

The FP800 agricultural drone from TopXGun Robotics drew the attention of many visitors and buyers at the drone industry zone.

The FP800 has a maximum payload of 85 kilograms and is equipped with an 80-liter spraying tank and a 120-liter spreading tank, Zheng Donghua, overseas sales engineer of TopXGun, told Yicai. The drone can perform four core tasks: crop protection spraying, fertilizer spreading, seed sowing, and material lifting, making it very popular among farmers in South America's agricultural regions, Zheng added.

The all-domain intelligent perception system of the FP800 enables precise obstacle avoidance and uniform spraying, helping farmers significantly improve pesticide and fertilizer utilization rates while reducing resource waste, Zheng pointed out.

A representative from Chengzhi Intelligent Machinery Technology introduced the company's new products to Yicai, including the NV10 photoelectric night vision binocular. The product delivers a clear and accurate picture even in darkness, haze, or backlit conditions. It also supports real-time image transmission and remote collaborative operation and can be used in various scenarios, including criminal investigation, border patrol, critical-area surveillance, and emergency rescue, the representative pointed out.

PadBot Robotics attracted many overseas buyers at its exhibition area, with some foreign influencers stopping to take photos with its robots.

One of PadBot's best-selling robots on display can autonomously plan optimal routes and avoid various obstacles in real time, Deputy General Manager Shu Xuqiong said to Yicai, adding that it can also charge itself, allowing it to operate for long periods without human intervention.

The robot can also identify various environmental anomalies in real time, automatically capturing on-site images and sending incident alerts through the management backend, phone calls, and text messages, Shu noted.

The first phase of the Fall Canton Fair runs from Oct. 15 to 19, with the second phase held from Oct. 23 to 27 under the theme "Quality Home Living" and the third, themed "Better Life," from Oct. 31 to Nov. 4. About 86,000 overseas buyers from 208 countries and regions attended the fair yesterday, while their total number for the entire event is expected to top 340,000.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: DeepSeek Offers Compensation After Nearly Five-Hour Outage
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 16 -- Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek has apologized for the latest application programming interface outage of nearly five hours, offering users full compensation.

Each user will receive a different compensation amount based on their API spending during the week of Oct. 8 to Oct. 14, DeepSeek said in an apology letter yesterday. Compensation varied from a few Chinese cents to over CNY1,000 (USD149), according to social media posts shared by users.

From 8.11 a.m. to 1.04 p.m. yesterday, DeepSeek experienced one of its largest service disruptions this year. Because it was a weekday morning in China, the issue seriously affected some developers and enterprises relying on the DeepSeek API.

DeepSeek has not yet revealed the cause of the outage but said in the apology letter that it has already launched an investigation into service stability and carried out a thorough overhaul, including “identifying and removing single-point dependencies,” to prevent similar problems from happening again.

So far this year, DeepSeek has experienced at least 10 major outages, including reports of “service unavailable” and “service abnormal,” as well as frequent complaints of “performance degradation.” Some industry analysts believe that yesterday’s crash may have been caused by a shortage in computing power supply.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Chinese Futures Market to List New Varieties, Further Open Up During 15th Five-Year Plan Period
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 16 -- The Chinese futures market will promote the listing of new varieties and steadily expand its opening-up to the outside world during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), according to officials.

The futures market will steadily expand the opening-up of specific futures varieties, deepen overseas authorization of settlement prices and cross-border delivery cooperation, strengthen risk control along the entire chain, and crack down on illegal and irregular behaviors, Zhang Yue, deputy director of the China Securities Regulatory Commission's futures supervision department, said at the Shanghai Derivatives Market Forum yesterday.

During the 15th Five-Year Plan period, the Shanghai Futures Exchange will strengthen its competitive products, such as metals, energy, and shipping, promote the listing of liquefied natural gas and fluting medium futures and options, advance the development of electricity and other varieties, gradually promote the opening-up of platforms, services, and other fields, and expand the application scenarios of the Shanghai Price, said Tian Xiangyang, Party secretary and chairman of the SHFE.

The SHFE has opened 11 specific varieties to overseas traders and 47 varieties to qualified foreign investors, basically covering all its listed varieties. It also authorized the London Metal Exchange to use its hot-rolled coil futures settlement price to develop related contracts and launched a cross-border delivery business for the No. 20 rubber futures, the first of its kind.

To serve the real economy, the SHFE has launched arbitrage and market orders and listed five options this year. As of Aug. 31, more than 360 Chinese mainland-listed real economy firms had announced their participation in SHFE varieties, an increase of more than 20 percent from a year earlier.

During the 15th Five-Year Plan period, the China Financial Futures Exchange will focus on enhancing the internal stability of the market and make front-line supervision more scientific, promoting the diversification of the participant structure, strengthening the completeness of product systems, and steadily expanding opening-up, said He Qingwen, Party secretary and chairman of the CFFEX.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: ByteDance's Seed to Form New Unit to Tackle Advanced AI Risks
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 13 -- TikTok owner ByteDance's artificial intelligence research team Seed plans to establish a dedicated department to strengthen AI safety and alignment as models become increasingly capable and autonomous.

Seed will be the first frontier AI laboratory in China to establish such a department, The Paper reported today. Named Seed Model-Alignment & Preparedness, the new unit will focus on ensuring that AI models behave in accordance with human intentions and safety constraints.

The department will step up investment in improving the safety of AI agent models and preventing risks associated with advanced chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear capabilities, according to the report.

It will also seek to reduce the risks of misuse and unintended model behavior as AI capabilities and autonomy advance, while building a comprehensive safety framework to address emerging and unforeseen threats.

Citing an internal company email, The Paper reported that the department will continue investing in model specifications, safety assessment systems, alignment training, protective mechanisms, and risk monitoring. It will also strengthen open collaboration with external research institutions and third-party evaluators.

The ultimate goal is to ensure that advanced AI models can effectively carry out tasks while operating within safety and authorization constraints, the email said.

Founded in 2023, Seed researches multimodal large language models, generative media, AI for science, and robotics, with the aim of advancing artificial general intelligence, according to ByteDance's website. The team has laboratories and job openings in China, Singapore, and the United States.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: Chinese EV Giant BYD Enters Namibian Market in Global Expansion Drive
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 7 -- Chinese automaker BYD has officially launched its new energy vehicle brand in Namibia, expanding its presence in the African market.

Namibian automotive distributor Pupkewitz Motors announced yesterday that it will represent BYD in the country, with the brand to be offered through retail outlets in Windhoek, Walvis Bay and Ongwediva.

"Our ambition is not simply to introduce new vehicles to the market, but to create an experience around new energy mobility that is relevant to Namibian customers. We look forward to building awareness, educating consumers and allowing customers to experience BYD for themselves," said Nico Pieters, a franchise executive at Pupkewitz Motors, in a statement.

Models being introduced to the Namibian market include the BYD Dolphin, BYD Dolphin Surf, BYD Sealion 5, BYD Sealion 6, BYD Shark 6, BYD Sealion 7 and BYD Seal Performance.

"The range allows Namibian customers to explore different forms of electrified mobility while experiencing the technology, comfort and features associated with the BYD brand," Pieters said.

He said the launch comes as energy efficiency, sustainability and the future of transportation gain increasing attention globally.

"BYD's global focus on new energy technologies places the brand at the forefront of this changing automotive landscape, while its entry into Namibia provides local motorists with greater access to alternative vehicle technologies," he added.

With the official launch of BYD, Pupkewitz Motors is expanding its portfolio to include a global new energy vehicle brand, reinforcing its commitment to providing Namibian customers with greater choice as mobility evolves.

In September, economic and market indicators from Namibian firm IJG Securities, showed that Chinese brands are steadily gaining popularity in Namibia. Haval, Jetour and Chery accounted for 5.9 percent, 5.8 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively, of the Namibian passenger vehicle market.

Editor: Dou Shicong

data.title: Chinese Appliance Giants Step Up Investment in Egypt, Thailand Despite Tariff Swings
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 16 -- Leading Chinese home appliance firms, including Haier Smart Home and Midea Group, are increasing investment in their overseas factories in countries such as Egypt and Thailand, saying tariff fluctuations have not changed their long-term localization plans.

Regardless of tariff changes, only a long-term global presence can give a company the confidence to minimize risks, Hu Tianshuai, head of international public relations and communications at Midea, told Yicai at the 140th China Import and Export Fair, better known as the Canton Fair, in China’s southern Guangzhou yesterday.

Midea has just set up an oven factory in Egypt, its seventh in the country, and the Egyptian base as a whole can meet demand from Africa and the Middle East, Hu noted, adding that the firm has also expanded its research and development center in the US, is developing a factory in Mexico, and has set up plants in Vietnam and Thailand.

Haier will break ground at a washing machine factory in Thailand on Oct. 26, and the second phase of its refrigerator and freezer plant at its industrial park in Egypt will open in mid-to-late November, Yicai learned from the company staff at the Canton Fair.

Haier will add factories and expand capacity in South Asia and rebuild its integrated research, manufacturing, and sales network in South America, Brazil, and Algeria, Zhang Qingfu, vice president of the firm’s overseas home appliance subsidiary, told Yicai at the Canton Fair.

Vanward New Electric’s production base in Thailand can serve Southeast Asia, Europe, and the United States, while the one in Egypt can cover Africa, the Middle East, and also Europe, Yang Songwen, VP of the Chinese water heater and kitchen appliance maker, told Yicai at the Canton Fair. He attended the groundbreaking ceremony for the second phase of Vanward’s Egyptian base on earlier this month.

Once the second phase of its Egyptian base is completed, Vanward will have a local annual output capacity of two million sets of gas water heater components and 500,000 finished units. Meanwhile, its Thai base already has an annual capacity of three million kitchen appliances, outdoor grills, and other products.

Setting up production bases overseas helps Chinese companies avoid trade barriers, reduces the impact of tariffs, and shortens delivery times, Yang noted. Easing tariffs between China and the US will improve the business environment, but it will not affect Vanward's global expansion because localization is true globalization, and only win-win cooperation with local industrial chains can bring long-term growth, he added.

The overseas sales head at a Chinese cleaning appliance maker told Yicai at the Canton Fair that it already has factories in Vietnam and Thailand and has moved production of some US-bound products there. Frequent changes in US tariff policy are a major challenge, so the company hopes tariffs will remain stable, the head pointed out.

Deepening Localization

Demand in Thailand is completely different from that in China, Yang said. Gas water heaters and storage-type electric water heaters dominate in China, but in Thailand, people use instant water heaters, he explained.

Vanward's Egyptian project is wholly owned and not only serves the local market but also the Middle East and Europe. It supplies components such as heat exchangers, burners, and valve bodies to local and international brands. The company has teamed up with dozens of supply chain partners in Thailand and more than 10 in Egypt.

The supply chains and talent teams at Vanward’s overseas production bases are becoming increasingly localized, as its headquarters mainly provides strategy and compliance requirements, Yang noted.

Companies should not put all their eggs in one basket, Hu said. Even if some regional markets fluctuate, others still offer opportunities, she pointed out, adding that Midea's business in Asia-Pacific and Latin America is growing quickly, and its expansion will follow local demand.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: DeepSeek Suffers Nearly Five-Hour AI Service Outage, One of Its Worst This Year
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 15 -- Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek today suffered one of its most serious service outages this year, disrupting its chatbot and application programming interface services for nearly five hours during peak working hours.

The incident lasted from 8:11 a.m. to 1:04 p.m. Beijing time, affecting DeepSeek's web platform and mobile app. Many users reported work disruptions on social media. The Hangzhou-based startup, known for its low-cost open-source models, has not responded to Yicai's inquiry about the cause as of press time.

Affected services included chat functions, DeepSeek V4.1 Pro API, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash API, according to the company's official service status page. DeepSeek said at 9:06 a.m. that the root cause had been identified and repairs were underway. At 12:49 p.m., it updated the status to “Repair completed, results under monitoring,” before announcing “Service restored” at 1:04 p.m.

DeepSeek had about 129 million monthly active users as of June, ranking third among China's AI-native apps, according to a first-half market report released by research firm QuestMobile.

The company also ranked 14th among AI apps worldwide and fifth among AI websites by monthly active users, according to a report published earlier this month by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, also known as a16z.

DeepSeek's official service status records show at least 10 incidents since the beginning of the year, ranging from service outages to performance degradation. A previous prolonged disruption occurred on Sept. 15, when its web platform and API services were partially unavailable for about three hours.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Emmi Laine

data.title: Robots Show Off Improved Intelligence at 26th China International Industry Fair
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 13 -- Robots at the 26th China International Industry Fair, which kicked off yesterday, are visibly more flexible than those that clumsily grabbed items at the year-earlier edition, with their intelligence continuing to improve.

Compared with collaborative robots that rely on programming, embodied intelligence with a brain and a hardware body has generalizable capabilities to learn, be trained, and evolve in real work scenarios, Chang Li, vice president of leading Chinese robot maker JAKA Robotics, told Yicai. "It can understand human instructions and quickly decompose tasks in the brain."

The trend of applying and popularizing embodied intelligence in many unstructured scenarios is inevitable, Chang noted during the debut of JAKA's wheeled humanoid robot at the fair, which autonomously moved boxes in a designated area of the exhibition hall.

JAKA is showcasing more than 30 robots at this year's CIIF, with about 60 percent being embodied intelligence products. More intelligent robots are entering diverse industrial application scenarios.

As more computing power and algorithm teams join the development, robots have gained stronger brains and become more flexible, a staff from Singapore starup RoboSpec said to Yicai. "Robots grab things as fast as humans do," the person noted, adding that one is making its global debut at the CIIF.

Traditional industrial robots suit standardized work scenarios, as they can deliver faster speeds and higher efficiency, but embodied intelligence is better for non-standard scenarios, Hua Zenan, a senior engineer at a foreign traditional industrial robot firm, told Yicai. As embodied intelligence tech advances, the two segments are gradually merging, and leading companies are expanding into humanoid robots, Hua pointed out.

AI-driven industrial automation is not about "reducing manpower" but about "reducing workload," Liu Wen, head of Schneider Electric's Industrial Automation Business' Digital Capability Center in China, said to Yicai. On the one hand, it frees people from repetitive labor and dangerous situations, allowing production personnel to shift to more valuable roles, and on the other, it helps reduce accidents and improve manufacturing stability and quality, Liu stressed.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: L’Oréal, Medtronic CEOs, Other Global Business Leaders Set to Attend This Year’s CIIE
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 15 -- With the 2026 China International Import Expo fast approaching, senior executives from L’Oréal, Medtronic and other multinational companies have confirmed to Yicai that they will attend the event in person, viewing it as an opportunity to strengthen ties with local customers and business partners.

Geoff Martha, chairman and chief executive officer of American-Irish medical device company Medtronic, has confirmed to Yicai that he will lead a delegation of senior executives to this year’s expo. This will be his first time attending the CIIE.

The CIIE is not only an important platform for showcasing products, but also a valuable opportunity for Dublin-based Medtronic to have in-depth exchanges with patients, partners and policy makers in the most dynamic healthcare market in the world, Martha said.

Nicolas Hieronimus, CEO of French cosmetics giant L’Oréal, has also confirmed that he will return to Shanghai with the company’s global management team to attend this year’s CIIE. For Hauts-de-Seine-based L’Oréal, the CIIE is far more than an annual event. It is an important platform for global collaboration and exchange, he said.

Frank Hammes, global CEO of Swiss air-quality technology firm IQAir, Franck Marilly, global CEO of French spirits group Rémy Cointreau, and Stéphane de La Faverie, president and CEO of US beauty company Estée Lauder have all confirmed that they will travel to Shanghai to attend the expo and participate in related events.

The CIIE provides global businesses with valuable opportunities to strengthen existing partnerships and explore new areas of cooperation, Marilly said. China is an important market for the group’s global growth and an indispensable part of its long-term strategic plans.

China is not only one of Estée Lauder’s most important markets globally, but is also an increasingly important source of talents, consumer insights and inspiration for the group, de La Faverie said. The experience and innovative practices that Estée Lauder develops here help the New York-based company to better serve consumers around the world. This is why the firm continues to invest in China, he added.

The CIIE serves as an important platform for bringing together innovative ideas from around the world, connecting businesses with consumers and partners, and turning innovation into opportunities for growth, de La Faverie added.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Kim Taylor

data.title: China’s Geely, Nio Strengthen Battery-Swap Alliance With Cross-Shareholding Deal
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 28 -- Chinese automotive giant Geely Holding Group and electric vehicle manufacturer Nio will deepen their strategic cooperation on battery swapping and EV charging through a cross-shareholding arrangement at the subsidiary level, aimed at accelerating the expansion of their battery-swap and charging service networks.

Geely will use its 100 percent equity in its battery-swap service provider Yiyi Internet Technology and CNY640 million (USD95.3 million) in cash to subscribe to newly issued shares in Nio’s battery-swap and charging unit Nio Power, Shanghai-based Nio said today. Upon completion of the transaction, Geely will hold a 30 percent stake in Nio Power, which will have a post-investment valuation of CNY16 billion (USD2.4 billion).

Nio was one of the earliest Chinese EV manufacturers to adopt battery swapping and set up Nio Power in 2017 to develop and run a battery-swap and charging service network. As of Sept. 20, Nio operated 4,099 battery-swap stations and 5,289 charging stations, and had provided users with over 120 million battery swaps in total, it said.

Yiyi, founded in 2017, managed more than 470 battery-swap stations in over 40 cities across China as of April last year, and has plans to expand to 2,000 stations by next year, according to its website.

The integration of Yiyi into Nio Power will accelerate the expansion of Nio's battery swapping network, with the aim of building 10,000 battery-swap stations by 2030, Nio said. The two sides will also work together to establish unified battery-swapping technology standards, while Hangzhou-based Geely will develop battery-swap vehicles models for consumers.

Nio will also acquire a stake in Geely’s EV charging service provider Zhejiang Haohan Energy Technology, according to the agreement between the two parties. Upon completion of the transaction, Nio will hold a 10 percent stake in Haohan, and both sides will share resources to expand charging network coverage and improve operational efficiency.

Haohan currently operates 2,500 charging stations and 12,000 charging guns in 232 cities across China. By the end of 2027, it plans to expand its network to 22,000 charging stations and 100,000 charging guns, Geely said.

The collaboration between Nio and Geely dates back to November 2023, when Nio announced plans to form a battery swapping alliance with automakers. Since then, it has established partnerships with eight automakers, including Changan Automobile and Geely.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: Low Fares, More Flexible Services Revive Intercity Bus Travel in China
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 15 -- China’s intercity bus operators have found a way to regain passengers for shorter journeys by competing on price, convenience, service flexibility, and operating efficiency.

The intercity bus sector slumped from the late 2010s as the expansion of the nation’s high-speed rail network and rising private car ownership eroded demand, with routes suspended and bus stations shuttered. The pandemic delivered a further blow in the early 2020s. Now, some operators are winning back passengers.

The examples of Yangyang Bus in the Pearl River Delta region and Leopard Transportation in the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region suggest that lower fares, stops closer to passengers’ homes, more frequent departures, online booking, and demand-based scheduling can make buses attractive again for commuters, students, family visits, and short leisure trips.

Passenger load factors on Yangyang Bus’s main routes exceed 70 percent during off-peak periods and climb to 90 percent to 100 percent in peak hours on work days and at weekends, Zhang Peng, its operations manager, told Yicai.

Yangyang Bus mainly caters to intercity commuters, university and college students, people visiting relatives, and travellers taking short leisure trips, Zhang said. It serves more than 12,000 passengers a day on average, with daily volumes reaching a peak of 30,000 to 35,000 during public holidays.

Competitive fares are one of the main reasons passengers are returning. “From the provincial capital Guangzhou to Shenzhen, our tickets cost less than CNY20 (USD3), while high-speed train fares cost CNY70 to CNY80,” Zhang pointed out. Even during holidays, bus fares stay the same.

Better service is another draw. Traditional long-distance transportation means require passengers to buy tickets at bus stations and then wait there, Zhang said. But now, some intercity bus services stop near metro entrances, business districts, and residential neighborhoods, allowing passengers to board closer to home.

Online ticketing platforms have also made bus travel much more convenient. Passengers can buy tickets just an hour before departure during peak holiday periods and still get a seat. High-speed train tickets can be difficult to secure at such short notice.

Cheaper and More Often

Leopard Transportation’s new express bus service has won passengers back after lowering fares and shortening departure intervals, Han Xiaolei, its deputy general manager, told Yicai.

On the route between Yinchuan and Wuzhong, for example, the fare was cut to CNY12 from CNY20 when the express service was launched, and departures increased in frequency to every 30 minutes from one hour, and then to every 20 minutes. The service now makes 70 round trips a day, with high passenger loads.

Leopard Transportation now operates 12 such express routes, with more than 420 buses serving over 12,000 passengers daily, Han noted, adding that their average load factor is about 80 percent and can rise to 95 percent during holidays.


The two bus operators’ new business models have something in common. Rather than relying on passengers to come to bus stations, they bring services closer to where people live and travel, while using real-world big data to determine how much capacity to deploy.

“We don’t make high profits from a single ticket, but mainly rely on improving load factors and reducing empty runs,” Zhang explained. Yangyang Bus cuts the number of buses in operation during periods with fewer passengers, he said, adding that it maintains both an in-house fleet while also partnering with other fleet operators, allowing otherwise idle vehicles to be put to use during seasonal or other downturns in demand.

The ability to attract passengers is crucial for transport service providers, Han said. Lower fares and stops closer to passengers may be the first steps towards winning customers back. But ultimately companies must ensure that each bus carries enough people and that every vehicle is used as efficiently as possible.


Editors: Tang Shihua, Futura Costaglione

data.title: China's Tianyuan Rises on USD68.7 Million Plan to Build Compound Semiconductor Material Plant in Yunnan
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 15 -- Tianyuan Group rose after the Chinese provider of energy-saving and environmental protection services said it plans to invest CNY500 million (USD68.7 million) building a high-purity indium phosphide and high-purity indium factory in Yunnan province, a southern region rich in upstream raw material resources, to capture new opportunities brought by the computing infrastructure boom.

Tianyuan [SHE: 301127] closed 2.5 percent higher at CNY14.70 (USD2.20) a share today, after surging by as much as 10 percent at one point. Chinese stocks were under selling pressure during the whole day, with Shenzhen's tech-focused ChiNext Index falling 2.9 percent.

The project will be located in the zero-carbon park within the Chuxiong High-Tech Industrial Development Zone, with the base having an annual production capacity of 100 tons of indium phosphide polycrystal products and 200 tons of 6N/7N-grade high-purity indium, Wuhan-based Tianyuan said in a stock exchange filing late yesterday. Construction should take 12 months.

The administrative committee of Chuxiong High-Tech Industrial Development Zone pledged to help Tianyuan establish a long-term and stable alliance with producers of high-purity phosphorus and crude indium in the zone to secure raw material supply for the project, the company noted. Indium phosphide polycrystal is synthesized using high-purity indium and high-purity phosphorus as raw materials.

Yunnan boasts abundant crude indium resources. Crude indium is a byproduct recovered during the smelting of non-ferrous metals such as zinc and lead, with high-purity indium refined from crude indium.

Tianyuan entered the emerging semiconductor materials industry in August after acquiring a 60 percent stake in Zhongxun Semiconductor Jiangsu, a startup researching and developing compound semiconductor substrate materials including indium phosphide, according to its latest earnings report. Zhongxun has mastered production technologies for optoelectronic semiconductor materials such as indium phosphide single crystal, though it has yet to generate operating revenue.

Indium phosphide single crystal is produced from indium phosphide polycrystal. Further processing yields indium phosphide substrates with excellent photoelectric conversion properties. The substrates serve as the core base material for high-speed optical communication lasers, radio-frequency devices, and infrared optoelectronic chips, the latter of which are core components packaged inside high-speed optical modules.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: WeChat Launches Mini-Program to Rival ByteDance’s Short Drama App
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 15 -- Tencent Holdings has launched a short drama mini-program on its super app WeChat to rival ByteDance’s short drama app Hongguo.

Lvpaopao offers free content and earns money from advertisements between episodes. It does not produce content itself, as third-party producers and authorized distributors provide all short dramas. WeChat users do not need to download any apps and can watch the short dramas on the mini-program directly.

High-quality short dramas co-distributed by Lvpaopao with an average play duration of over 10 minutes per person can receive revenue incentives of up to 100 percent, of which 90 percent in cash dividends and 10 percent in advertising bonuses, according to the Lvpaopao mini-program. The threshold for the incentives is based on view duration rather than view counts.

Users’ view duration on Lvpaopao is about five times that of the overall market, and its retention rate is more than 2.5 times, according to statistics released by WeChat.

Hongguo had about 168 million users in July, up 107 percent from a year earlier, higher than long-form video platforms Tencent Video, iQiyi, Youku, and Mango TV combined, which is about 155 million users, according to the latest monitoring data from Chinese internet big data company QuestMobile.

WeChat launched Lvpaopao not as a proactive attack but as a form of traffic integration, an industry insider said, The Paper reported. Mini-programs of companies such as Jiuzhou Culture Media and Dianzhong Tech invested in advertising on WeChat, and WeChat earned advertising fees, so after they cut their investment in advertising, WeChat decided to enter this business to maintain advertising revenue, the insider explained.

In the short term, Lvpaopao is unlikely to bring significant changes to the industry, as producers will have to keep balancing revenue sharing across platforms, and users have already gotten used to Hongguo, a leading short drama producer said. In the long run, if WeChat relies heavily on channels such as ‌WeChat Channels to attract users, there is still a chance for Lvpaopao to stand out.

Users have very private and personal preferences when it comes to short dramas, said Han Jiazheng, professor at the School of Animation and Digital Arts at Communication University of China. Lvpaopao would let users’ WeChat friends see what they are watching, which could raise privacy concerns and create a social-psychological burden, making users less willing to watch dramas on the mini-program, Han explained.

Both Lvpaopao and Hongguo consider artificial intelligence-generated short dramas as their core business. Founder Securities believes that higher-quality, globalized, AI-generated content is the core theme of short dramas this year.

AI-generated lifelike simulation dramas have become the main driving force for platforms to attract users and release new products, with view counts exceeding the total of all AI-generated and animated short dramas in previous years.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: China's LandSpace Sends 10 New Satellites Into Space
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 15 -- LandSpace Technology, a private Chinese rocket launch service provider, has put eight compute test satellites and two communications test satellites into their planned orbits, adding to the 10 satellites it sent into space less than a month ago.

The Zhuque-2E, an upgraded version of the Zhuque-2 rocket, launched yesterday carrying eight compute satellites developed by Guoxing Aerospace Technology and two next-generation laser data transmission test satellites developed by Lanta Intelligence.

The Zhuque-2E is a two-stage cryogenic extended liquid carrier rocket powered by liquid oxygen-methane propellant, with a payload capacity of six tons to low Earth orbit and four tons to a 500-kilometer sun-synchronous orbit. The same type of rocket placed 10 low-Earth-orbit internet satellites into orbit on Sept. 15.

The new launch was not only another successful payload deployment, but also a demonstration of Zhuque-2's ability to support the construction of space infrastructure, such as compute satellite constellations, Ma Haijing, general manager of LandSpace's marketing department, told Yicai. The success means the rocket can provide launch services for deploying space-based computing constellations, marking a breakthrough in the firm's commercial services in this emerging field, Ma stressed.

The eight compute satellites are the first in the Group 02 constellation Guoxing Aerospace sends for tech verification of its space computing network. China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation launched the 12 satellites in Group 01 of the program into orbit last May.

The two Lanta Intelligence satellites are intended to verify its key satellite networking technologies. Zhuque-2E also launched the first two satellites in this program in November 2024, which have since completed multiple on-orbit technology verification tests.

The rideshare launch model, which combines satellites of different types from different customers on a single rocket, offers customers a more flexible way to access space, Ma pointed out. By coordinating launch demand from multiple clients, LandSpace can make full use of the rocket's payload capacity and fairing space, improve payload utilization efficiency on each launch, and help create conditions to lower customers' overall launch costs, Ma said.

The upgraded Zhuque-2 is one of the key rocket models LandSpace uses for routine commercial launch missions, while the company's reusable Zhuque-3 rocket is designed to meet launch demands requiring greater payload capacity and higher launch frequency. In August, the Zhuque-3 became China's first launch vehicle to both place a satellite into orbit and complete a first-stage land recovery.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev
